body:
This seems like the engine doesn't gracefully handle invalid use, the RIDs naturally don't persist between runs

I'm not sure what would be best to do here when the user assigns some invalid texture

> This seems like the engine doesn't gracefully handle invalid use, the RIDs naturally don't persist between runs

I understood that they do not persist. In the MRP, however, the RID should have got re-assigned when the scene is re-opened, since it is the compositor effect (ce.gd in MRP) which is modifying it.

Considering the fact that re-assigning the Texture#DRD to the material would resolve the problem, I guesstimate that the problem lies somewhere else, most likely the setter function of texture_rd_rid.

I also do Texture2DRD.texture_rd_rid = RID() in the PREDELETE notification in the compositor effect here, so closing it would (should) clear the rid (and I don't think anything related to saving needs to be handled here, the texture_rd_rid field shouldn't be hinted as storage, right? It doesn't show up in the .tres file even if I do not clear the RID in code).

And the engine is, indeed, not very gracefully handling invalid use here - failing to set it to RID() when the CE is deleted would end up flooding the terminal with error messages (I guess this may be reported as another issue, so I just left some comments in the code of MRP).
